Chapter 3: The Wild Man Within and the Journey of Initiation
You know, there comes a moment in all our lives when the world we’ve always known just... slips away. Sometimes, it’s a quiet call—a nagging sense that something’s missing, maybe a craving for adventure, or just a feeling that a piece of us got left behind. Other times, it hits hard. A crisis, a loss, or a sudden change might shake everything up, leaving us standing in the rubble of old certainties.
In the story of Iron John, this turning point comes when the young prince, driven by curiosity—and maybe a secret sense of kinship—unlocks the cage and sets the wild man free.
Now, think of the wild man. He’s rough, untamed, and a little intimidating. But really, he stands for the parts of ourselves we’ve locked away—our raw feelings, instincts, and those deep-down desires that just don’t fit in with what’s considered “proper.” Most of us learn early on to hide these parts, to keep them under wraps. But here’s the kicker: when we shut away the wild man inside, life starts to lose its spark. Everything becomes... predictable. And often, it just feels empty.
The true journey—the journey of initiation—begins the moment the prince leaves the comfort of the palace to follow the wild man into the forest. This isn’t just about wandering into the trees; it’s a leap into the unknown. It means facing fears and old wounds we’ve tried to bury for years.
Long ago, this journey was marked by real rituals. Boys were taken from their mothers, taught by older men, and challenged to prove themselves. These rites of passage helped break childhood’s hold and prepared them for the responsibilities of adult life.
But today? Most of us make this journey alone. There aren’t many mentors, and the rituals have faded. So a lot of men stumble through it, unsure what’s happening or even why it matters. The wild man, who once guided and taught, now feels like a stranger—maybe even someone to fear or ignore. But the need for that initiation is still there. Without it, so many of us drift, searching for meaning in work or relationships, or numbing ourselves with distractions, always feeling like something’s missing.
Take the story of one man. He felt trapped in a job he couldn’t stand, and anger kept bubbling up—at work, at home, even in his dreams. He kept trying to push it down. But finally, he looked at his own story, at all the ways he’d learned to hide his feelings and always play it safe. That’s when he realized—the wild man inside was calling out, desperate to be heard.
Or think of another man, struggling with depression. He found himself wandering the woods, just listening to the wind and birds. Out there, he felt a peace he couldn’t find anywhere else. Over time, he saw that the wildness outside mirrored something inside him—a part he’d forgotten, but that was alive, creative, and deeply connected to the world.
The journey of initiation isn’t the same for everyone, but there are patterns. There’s usually a period of confusion or loss—a time when the old ways fall away and nothing feels certain. This is the “dark forest,” the place where we’re tested and transformed. It’s not comfortable, but it’s where real growth happens.
In the story, the prince faces a series of challenges—fetching water from a well, caring for the wild man, and meeting tasks that test his courage and creativity. But these aren’t just about proving how strong or clever he is. They’re about learning to trust himself, to face fear and uncertainty, and to discover strengths he didn’t know he had.
For many of us, the hardest part is letting go of the old roles—being the “good boy,” the “nice guy,” or the ever “responsible son.” Those roles might have protected us once, but after a while, they can feel like a cage. The wild man, with his fierce independence and deep wisdom, offers another way. He shows that real maturity isn’t about blindly following rules, but about finding your own path—bringing together your wildness and your wisdom to build a life that’s true and meaningful.
Look, this journey isn’t easy. It’s rarely straightforward. There will be setbacks, failures, and moments when you doubt everything. But every challenge is a chance to grow, to learn, and to become more fully yourself. The wild man—once feared and shut away—becomes a source of strength and guidance. He reminds us that becoming a man isn’t about being perfect. It’s about becoming whole.
And in a world that prizes control and fitting in, the call of the wild man matters more than ever. He invites us back to deeper rhythms, to the challenge and joy of being fully human. The story of Iron John, with its forests, cages, and wild men, becomes a guide for anyone willing to take the risk—to step out of safety and into the unknown.
